Measuring uncooked white rice

A cup of uncooked long-grain white rice weighs about 185 g. Short-grain and medium-grain rice pack a little tighter and weigh closer to 200 g per cup. Brown rice is about the same as white.

Rice roughly triples in volume when it cooks. One cup of dry rice makes about 3 cups cooked, and the weight goes up just as much because the grains absorb water. If you're counting portions or calories, make sure you know whether a recipe means dry or cooked.

Source: USDA FoodData Central (185 g, long-grain white, raw); King Arthur Baking lists 198 g.

Questions

How many grams is ½ cup of uncooked white rice?

½ cup of uncooked white rice weighs about 93 g (3.26 oz). A full cup is 185 g.

How many cups is 100 grams of uncooked white rice?

100 g of uncooked white rice is about ½ cup, based on 185 g per cup.

How much cooked rice does 1 cup of uncooked rice make?

About 3 cups. One cup (185 g) of dry long-grain white rice absorbs water as it cooks and ends up around 3 cups, or roughly 475 g.
